newsitem.title: INDIA: India police seize rare tiger skins.
newsitem.headline: India police seize rare tiger skins.

text.p: Calcutta police have arrested two men after seizing the skins of two rare Royal Bengal tigers worth $16,800, officials said on Tuesday.
Criminal Investigation Department deputy chief Partho Bhattacharya said police arrested a trader and his collaborator on Monday.
India is home to 60 percent of the world's surviving tigers which face extinction within a decade.
Wildlife experts say at least one of India's estimated 2,500 tigers is killed every day to feed a lucrative international trade in tiger bones, skins, nails, teeth and penises.

"We suspect that the two tigers have been killed recently and, most probably, the two were trapped and poisoned to death by the poachers since there was no sign of injury on the skins," Bhattacharya said.
